recommendation.summary: S6 transactional patch set of 3 function(s) (body-only change).
justification: no state-schema, dependency, toolchain, goroutine-structure or long-running-code change
every member of the patch set is an ordinary non-generic function or method, so each can be redirected through its slot, and the whole set is published in one atomic PatchSet store
alternatives: S2 Go plugin swap of the affected handler (same toolchain; old code leaks)
S1 epoch swap if v2 is compiled in alongside v1 (pre-staged release)
S5 FD-passing handoff (identity state transfer) or rolling update as fallback
risks: changed functions are small enough to be inlined; with S6 slot trampolines the call still dispatches through the slot, but raw binary patching (internal/livepatch) must also patch the inlining callers: github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.HeaderRoute.IsMatch, github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.compressResponseWriter.Close, github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.compressResponseWriter.Flush, github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.compressResponseWriter.Hijack, github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.compressResponseWriter.Push, github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.compressResponseWriter.Write
no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 3 functions
